items.title: Saber-toothed cats' spinal tumors suggest inbred species struggled to survive
items.summary: The fossilized spines of saber-toothed cats in the La Brea Tar Pits reveal evidence of an unexpectedly high prevalence of rare spinal nerve tumors, suggesting that the species became inbred just before extinction. items.title: Tigray's old grapevines have survived against the odds: New research uncovers their genetic and historic value
items.summary: The northern highlands of Ethiopia are among Africa's oldest agricultural landscapes. Some of the world's most important crops originated here, particularly pulses and grains, including teff. Yet another crop has a less well-known history in Ethiopia's Tigray region: the grapevine.

items.title: Forest productivity, not rapid warming, shapes Northern Eurasia's carbon sink
items.summary: Northern Eurasia contains about 20% of the world's forests and plays a crucial role in mitigating climate change by absorbing atmospheric carbon dioxide, thereby acting as a major carbon sink. items.title: Znanstvenici razvili uređaj koji usmjerava struju pomoću svjetlosti
items.summary: FIZIČARI su razvili uređaj, 'elektronički svjetionik', koji koristi svjetlost za stvaranje i usmjeravanje snopa elektrona bez vanjskog napajanja. Otkriće bi moglo unaprijediti kvantne tehnologije.

items.summary: By analyzing the data from NASA's Fermi gamma-ray space telescope, Chinese astronomers have investigated a recently identified millisecond pulsar known as PSR J0435+3233. items.title: A quantum heat engine that simultaneously provides work and refrigeration
items.summary: The laws of thermodynamics state that heat naturally flows from hotter systems or regions to colder systems or regions until a state of thermal equilibrium is reached. This simple principle underpins the operation of numerous technologies, ranging from refrigerators to power plants.

items.title: Je li prije ljudi na Zemlji postojala druga napredna civilizacija?
items.summary: ZNANSTVENICI istražuju 'Silurijansku hipotezu': bi li u geološkim zapisima Zemlje ostali tragovi napredne civilizacije koja je možda postojala i uništila se prije milijuna godina?

items.title: Znanstvenici: Kućni ljubimci mogući su izvor bakterija otpornih na lijekove
items.summary: NOVO istraživanje sugerira da kućni ljubimci mogu prenositi bakterije otporne na antibiotike na ljude zbog bliskog kontakta, s većim rizikom nego što je to slučaj sa stokom.

items.title: Američko-ruska svemirska posada vraća se na Zemlju nakon 8 mjeseci na ISS-u
items.summary: NAKON 241 dana na ISS-u, američko-ruska posada sigurno se vratila na Zemlju. Tijekom misije proveli su važna znanstvena istraživanja i pripremili postaju za buduće nadogradnje.

items.title: DNA vacuum captures animal traces from air to map Danish wildlife
items.summary: Researchers have developed a DNA vacuum that can suck genetic traces from animals out of the air and reveal which animals live in an area. items.title: The best way to save giant sequoias may be more fire
items.summary: Giant sequoias are built to withstand ordinary fires, but recent extreme wildfires killed thousands of trees that had survived for centuries or even millennia. items.title: Your AI calorie-tracking app may be off by 345 calories
items.summary: Popular AI-powered food apps may make calorie counting easier, but they may also leave out a surprisingly large part of the meal. items.title: Angola's oldest burials, including its only known ancient cremation, uncovered at a 15th-century site doomed by a dam
items.summary: As the construction of a hydroelectric dam loomed, archaeologists raced to uncover Angola's earliest dated burials and its only known cremation at a 15th-century settlement before it vanished beneath the water.

items.title: CRISPR makes prostate cancer vulnerable to immunotherapy
items.summary: Scientists used CRISPR to make prostate cancer cells easier for the immune system to detect and destroy. The experimental treatment dramatically improved the effects of immunotherapy in mice and may offer hope for other hard-to-treat tumors.

items.title: Why losing the wrong fat can trigger diabetes
items.summary: Scientists discovered that damaged fat cells can become inflamed, lose their ability to store lipids, and eventually vanish, disrupting the body’s metabolism. The findings show that diabetes can result not only from excess fat, but also from losing the healthy fat tissue the body needs.

items.summary: Concluding an eight-month science mission aboard the International Space Station, NASA astronaut Chris Williams returned to Earth on Sunday alongside Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev. items.title: As wildfires grip France and Spain, what are the risks from the smoke?
items.summary: What dangers does smoke from wildfires pose? Who is most at risk? Here are some answers to health questions often asked, especially now with fires in France and Spain.

items.title: A hidden Alzheimer’s tipping point may decide who gets dementia
items.summary: Scientists have identified a possible tipping point that helps determine whether Alzheimer’s-related brain changes lead to dementia. The key may lie in how the brain’s immune cells respond to plaques and tau, offering a promising new target for treatments designed to extend cognitive resilience.

items.title: Baltikom se širi "morski kanibal"
items.summary: INVAZIVNI rebraš *Mnemiopsis leidyi* širi se Baltikom, prijeteći ribarstvu i ekosustavu. Hrani se zooplanktonom i ribljim jajima, a kanibalizam mu pomaže preživjeti. Širenju pogoduje i hipoksija.

items.title: Scotland declares 'major' wildfire in Cairngorms national park
items.summary: Scottish firefighters fought a wildfire Saturday that was burning through Cairngorms National Park in the north, with authorities advising residents to evacuate.

items.title: Thousands crowd shelters as wildfires force exodus in France, Spain
items.summary: Thousands crowded into emergency shelters in France and Spain on Sunday after wildfires drove more than 300,000 people to flee their homes and vacation accommodations.

items.summary: The Backrooms began as a single eerie image of empty yellow rooms, but internet users transformed it into a vast fictional world that feels disturbingly real. items.title: Hidden genetic diversity helped inbred brown tree snakes conquer guam
items.summary: A notorious snake invasion that devastated Guam’s native birds may have succeeded because the reptiles carried hidden genetic advantages. items.title: Scientists trace the shocking origin of human eyes to an ancient “cyclops”
items.summary: Researchers say a tiny one-eyed ancestor that lived nearly 600 million years ago may have shaped the evolution of every vertebrate eye, including our own. They also found that its ancient median eye lives on today as the pineal gland, which helps synchronize our sleep with daylight.
